subject: TileWave: P95 latency regression and short-term fallback authorization
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@tilewave.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@tilewave.com
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: TileWave: sudden P95 latency regression for model-delta v5.2

Hi Tessa —

We started seeing a pronounced latency regression this morning on the flows that use model-delta v5.2. Metrics: p95 jumped from ~360ms (baseline) to ~1.18s at 08:40 PDT, p99 up to ~2.4s. Error rate is stable, so not a downstream timeout — requests are completing but with much higher per-token latency.

This is affecting our interactive assistants in production (about ~12k reqs/min), and a subset of customers are reporting timeouts in their frontend. Our SRE has attached a trace sample (tilewave-trace-0909.json) from 08:47 showing long KV cache misses and frequent re-compaction operations.

Ask: can Redwood perform an immediate short-term mitigation (fallback or pin to v5.1) while you investigate? We also need to understand SLA implications — if p95 stays >800ms we will need credits or an agreed exception window.

Can you confirm what you can do now and how long it will take?

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Director of Platform
TileWave

Attachments: tilewave-trace-0909.json (trace sample)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@tilewave.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TileWave: sudden P95 latency regression for model-delta v5.2

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the trace. I’m looping in SRE (Markus) and your AE (Laura) to coordinate.

Immediate options (short timeline):
- Option A: pin traffic to model-delta v5.1 (known previous good) — fast, low-risk, should restore p95 to baseline within ~5–15 minutes of switching.
- Option B: enable variant fallback (automatic fallback to the compact variant) — lowers accuracy slightly but may improve latency without a full rollback.
- Option C: conservative batching and KV cache parameters tightened for customer-specific route — lower throughput but may reduce p95 for requests with long context.

We need explicit authorization to change routing or pin versions for a customer-facing flow (this is a controlled action). Please confirm TileWave is OK with Option A (pin to v5.1) for a limited window; if yes, we’ll request approval from Redwood SRE/Product to execute and will include an SLO exception window in writing.

Markus — can you review the attached trace and advise how quickly we can pin traffic and what mitigations you’d recommend?

Laura — looping you for the business/credit side and to coordinate any communication to TileWave stakeholders.

– Tessa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@tilewave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TileWave: sudden P95 latency regression for model-delta v5.2

Thanks for looping me in. Quick read of the trace + service metrics: pattern looks like v5.2’s KV cache eviction threshold is being hit more aggressively for the request population TileWave runs (longer average prompt lengths), which forces frequent recomputation of key blocks and increases token-level latency.

Immediate recommendation:
- Activate Option A (pin to v5.1) for TileWave and keep v5.2 traffic diverted. Pinning will be done via our routing control plane and should be effective within 5–10 minutes; I’ll run a canary at 10% for 2 minutes then flip 100% if traces look clean.
- In parallel, experiment with conservative batching and increase the KV cache retention for v5.2 in a canary to see if we can address root cause without long-term rollback.

I will need explicit authorization to change their routing (internal ticket INC-7821 opened). Attaching a short trace excerpt I pulled (sre_trace_sample_20290912.json) showing the KV miss burst.

Risks: pinning to v5.1 will temporarily bypass any improvements from v5.2 (accuracy/latency tradeoffs), and if customers rely on a v5.2-only feature we’ll need to flag it.

If we get approval now I’ll perform the canary at ~10:20 PDT.

– Markus
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sre_trace_sample_20290912.json
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TileWave: sudden P95 latency regression for model-delta v5.2

Tessa / Markus —

From a customer-facing standpoint I support a pin to v5.1 for a limited window (to reduce user impact). I authorize an initial 6-hour fallback window starting when the switch is completed.

Business ask: if p95 is still >800ms beyond that window we should offer a prorated credit; I’ll prepare language for the customer. Please make sure we record the SLO exception window in the Console and include the incident tag (tilewave-0909).

Mina — please help ensure CSMs are looped and that this is tracked for the postmortem / credit calculation.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TileWave: sudden P95 latency regression for model-delta v5.2

Thanks — quick notes from product/ops perspective:
- Do not enable any automated rollback that would flip traffic back to v5.2 without manual sign-off from SRE + Triage lead.
- Mark the incident in the Console (incident tag + start time). Set TTL for the SLO exception to 6 hours from activation.
- Schedule an RCA meeting (30m) for 2029-09-16 with SRE, Product, and AE; add the incident doc link to the meeting invite. Template: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/template.

I’ll update the internal incident doc and post the action items after Markus confirms the canary.

— Mina
Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@tilewave.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Summary and actions — TileWave latency mitigation (model-delta)

Elena — quick summary and confirmation of actions taken per approvals above: 

What we did (10:20 PDT):
- Per AE approval we pinned TileWave traffic to model-delta v5.1. Canary at 10% for 2 minutes, then flipped to 100% at 10:24 PDT.
- SLO exception window authorized by Laura: 10:20 PDT — 16:20 PDT (6 hours). Logged in Console under incident tag tilewave-0909.
- Markus collected traces and attached the SRE excerpt (sre_trace_sample_20290912.json). Fallback activation log attached.

Immediate outcome: p95 returned to ~380ms within the canary window. We will monitor for the next 6 hours and leave the pin in place while we run the KV cache retention experiments on v5.2.

Next steps:
- RCA draft due 2029-09-16; meeting invite to follow from Mina.
- If p95 remains >800ms beyond the exception window we’ll discuss credits (Laura will prepare language).
- No automatic rollbacks will be performed; any deployment change back to v5.2 needs manual sign-off from SRE + Triage.

Elena — can you confirm TileWave sees stabilization on your side? If so, we’ll keep monitoring and close the active incident when both sides are comfortable.

Thanks again for the quick signal and the trace; will follow up with the incident doc and the HubSpot record.

— Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fallback_activation_log_20290912.txt, tilewave-impact-summary.pdf
